title: Plaza Theatre opens (modelled on Piccadilly Circus)
hook: A 1936 cinema with a dance floor for British soldiers stood where the metro now is
notes: First film The Broadway Melody, April 1936; built by grandsons of Attara Kacheri contractor Arcot Narrainswamy Mudaliar on land of their furniture business
story: In April 1936 Plaza screened its first film, The Broadway Melody. Brothers A. S. Krishnamoorthy and Rajamanickam Velu built it on land where they had run a furniture business, after travelling to Britain to study cinemas, and modelled it on Piccadilly Circus. It had a bar and a wooden dance floor used by British soldiers. The best balcony seats cost 1 rupee 12 annas.

title: The Ten Commandments runs 44 weeks at Plaza
hook: Schools brought children in droves; the Maharaja of Mysore got a private screening
notes: Year refers to the Maharaja screening; run start year not stated
story: The Ten Commandments ran for 44 straight weeks, the longest run in Plaza's history. Schools brought children in by the busload, and in 1959 a private screening was arranged for the Maharaja of Mysore, Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar, and his entourage.

title: Plaza's last film: Meet the Fockers
hook: The last show was 17 March 2005 — then the building was bought for a mall that was never allowed
notes: BBMP refused mall permission; land acquired for Namma Metro
story: Plaza's final show was Meet the Fockers on 17 March 2005. The family sold the theatre; a mining investor from Ballari wanted to build a shopping mall, but the city corporation refused permission. The land was acquired for Namma Metro instead.

title: MG Road metro station opens; old boulevard demolished
hook: The old MG Road boulevard was demolished to build this station
notes: Modern photo = 'Now' side of Then/Now; confirm licence on file page
story: MG Road metro station now stands on the old Plaza site. Building Namma Metro here meant demolishing the old MG Road boulevard.

title: South Parade renamed Mahatma Gandhi Road
hook: Until 26 Feb 1948 this road was South Parade — the social spine of a British garrison
notes: Coord is a midpoint of MG Road; image dated 1923 on Commons
story: Before independence this road was South Parade, the social spine of the British Cantonment, known for its bars, restaurants and shops. On 26 February 1948 it was renamed Mahatma Gandhi Road. The photograph shows people walking on South Parade, with St Andrew's seen across the parade grounds.

title: The Parade Ground: heart of the Cantonment (est. 1809)
hook: A military parade ground was the centre of the whole British town
notes: Map image = 1854 Plan of Bangalore; exact parade ground extent to georeference
story: The British formally established the Cantonment in 1809, north-east of Kempe Gowda's old market town. Its heart was the Parade Ground, and the Civil and Military Station grew up around it. The image is an 1854 plan of Bangalore.

title: Bangalore Central Jail
hook: This park was a prison — Vajpayee and Advani were jailed here during the 1975 Emergency
notes: Jail founding year not yet sourced
story: Before it was a park, this was the Bangalore Central Jail. The prison site was later redeveloped as Freedom Park.

title: Emergency: opposition leaders imprisoned
hook: Vajpayee and Advani were among the leaders held here in 1975
story: When the Emergency was proclaimed in 1975, several opposition leaders, including Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L. K. Advani, were arrested and jailed in this prison.

title: Freedom Park opens with a protest zone
hook: Part of the old jail is now set aside for protests
notes: Opened November 2008
story: The old jail reopened to the public as Freedom Park in November 2008, with part of it set aside for protests. It later hosted Anna Hazare's indefinite fast, backed by India Against Corruption, for the Lokpal bill.

title: Sampangi Lake drained
hook: A stadium sits on the bed of a lake that was drained in 1937
notes: Drained after neglect once Hesaraghatta piped water arrived
story: This stadium sits on the bed of Sampangi Lake. Once piped water arrived from Hesaraghatta, the lake was neglected, came to be seen as an environmental hazard, and was drained in 1937.

title: Sampangi Stadium inaugurated
hook: Opened by Maharaja Jayachamaraja Wadiyar as Sampangi Stadium
story: Built on the drained lakebed, the stadium was inaugurated in 1946 by Maharaja Jayachamaraja Wadiyar as Sampangi Stadium. It was later renamed after his father, Yuvaraja Kanteerava Narasimharaja Wadiyar.

title: Bangalore United Services Club founded
hook: An officers-only club of the British Empire
notes: Image c.1883 by Albert Thomas Watson (Penn)
story: Founded in 1868 as the Bangalore United Services Club, for officers of the British Empire. Its past members include the Maharaja of Mysore and Winston Churchill. The picture shows the club around 1883.

title: Winston Churchill's unpaid bill of Rs 13
hook: A ledger on display lists Winston Churchill's Rs 13 as an irrecoverable debt
notes: Add a second independent source before publishing
story: A ledger on display in the club's main building lies open at a page of 'irrecoverable debts' the club wrote off. One entry: Rs 13, owed by Winston Churchill.

title: Club opens to civilians and is renamed
hook: Officers only until 1946 — then civilians were let in
story: Civilians were admitted in 1946, and the United Services Club became the Bangalore Club. When permanent membership was last open, the waiting list ran to more than 30 years. The photograph is from 1902.

title: St Mark's Church built on the South Parade grounds
notes: Wikidata inception 1812; Commons captions say 1808 — resolve
story: St Mark's was built on the South Parade grounds of the Cantonment. Sources disagree on the date: Wikidata gives 1812, while several Wikimedia Commons captions say 1808. Pictured here in 1900 by C. H. Doveton.

title: Fire guts St Mark's
hook: On 17 Feb 1923 a short circuit burned the church — photographed by Kenneth Anderson
notes: 3 PD photos; congregation moved to St Andrew's temporarily
story: On 17 February 1923 a short circuit set St Mark's on fire, ravaging the building. The congregation had to worship elsewhere while it was restored. These photographs of the damage are by Kenneth Anderson.

title: St Marks c.1912 (Tuck's postcard)
notes: Good Then/Now candidate
story: St Mark's on a Tuck's postcard from around 1912, about a decade before the fire of 1923.

title: Public Offices completed
hook: Mysore's government offices moved into this building in 1868
notes: Site had boulders and ravines; 14-ft foundations
story: Completed in 1868 as the Public Offices, the building housed the Mysore government's secretariat. The site, chosen by Mark Cubbon facing the Cantonment parade grounds, was full of boulders and ravines, so the builders laid foundations fourteen feet deep. The 1890 photograph shows Cubbon's equestrian statue out front.

title: New elected cabinet sworn in amid jubilation
hook: 24 Oct 1947: crowds cheered as an elected cabinet was sworn in here
story: On 24 October 1947 a new cabinet of elected representatives was sworn in here, and Attara Kacheri became a scene of great public jubilation.

title: Chief Minister wants it demolished
hook: Kengal Hanumanthaiah wanted this colonial building torn down
notes: Image is early 1900s postcard
story: In the early 1950s Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah wanted Attara Kacheri demolished as a vestige of colonialism. It survived. After the legislature moved to Vidhana Soudha in 1956, the High Court took over the whole building.

title: Cubbon statue moved into Cubbon Park
hook: Mark Cubbon's statue outside this building was moved into the park
notes: CONFLICT: Attara Kacheri article says 2019; Cubbon Park article says 28 June 2020. ILN image dated 5 May 1866 on Commons (filename says 1861)
story: Mark Cubbon's equestrian statue, long a fixture at this building, was moved to the Band Stand inside Cubbon Park. Sources disagree on when: one Wikipedia article says 2019, another says 28 June 2020. The engraving shows the statue's inauguration, from the Illustrated London News.

title: Meade's Park laid out
hook: Cubbon Park was first named after someone else — Sir John Meade
notes: Image 1890
story: Laid out in 1870 under Major General Richard Sankey, the park was first called Meade's Park, after acting commissioner Sir John Meade. It was later renamed after Sir Mark Cubbon, the longest-serving commissioner. Photographed in 1890.

title: Renamed Sri Chamarajendra Park — nobody used it
hook: Officially renamed in 1927; almost a century later everyone still says Cubbon Park
story: In 1927, for the silver jubilee of Krishnaraja Wodeyar's rule, the park was officially renamed Sri Chamarajendra Park. The name never caught on, and people kept calling it Cubbon Park.

title: Museum founded inside the Cantonment jail
hook: Bangalore's museum started life in a jail building
notes: Jail location unknown — do NOT place at Freedom Park; attach to museum place as backstory
story: The museum was established in 1865 with guidance from Surgeon Edward Balfour, who had founded the museum in Madras. Its first home was the Cantonment's jail building. That was judged unsuitable, so a purpose-built museum was planned.

title: Museum building opens on Sydney Road
hook: Kasturba Road used to be Sydney Road
notes: Image 1890
story: The museum's own building opened in 1877 on what was then Sydney Road, today Kasturba Road. Photographed in 1890.

title: Queen Victoria statue unveiled by future George V
hook: 5 Feb 1906: the Prince of Wales unveiled it on his India tour
notes: Modern photo 2004
story: Unveiled on 5 February 1906 by the Prince of Wales, the future King George V, during his tour of British India. From Bangalore he went on to Karachi to unveil yet another statue of the late queen.

title: Edward VII statue unveiled by Viceroy Chelmsford
notes: Image 1914 sculptor's plate
story: The statue of King Edward VII was unveiled in November 1919 by the Viceroy, Lord Chelmsford. The picture shows Leonard Jennings's marble statue as published in 1914.

title: Two auditoriums built on Brigade Road
notes: Coordinate is 202 Brigade Road (OSM) — confirm Rex address
story: In the late 1930s Rao Saheb Pasupalety Venugopal Naidu bought an acre on Brigade Road and built two auditoriums, which began screening films in the 1940s.

title: Reopens as Rex with Sleeping Beauty
hook: Won at auction in 1961 for Rs 8.51 lakh
story: After being mortgaged in 1951, the property was won at auction by Nand Lal Kapur in 1961. It opened as Rex in 1962 with The Sleeping Beauty, got air conditioning in 1971, and later ran Cliffhanger for 29 weeks.

title: Rex's final show
hook: 80 years of cinema ended on 31 Dec 2018
notes: Replaced by Prestige/Kapur multiplex
story: Rex shut on 31 December 2018 after about 80 years of cinema on the site. Kapur Investments and the Prestige Group planned a four-screen multiplex with shops and restaurants in its place.

title: Victoria Hotel demolished
hook: A one-acre colonial bungalow hotel stood where Bangalore Central mall is
notes: Coordinate is road-level placeholder; confirm mall location
story: Victoria Hotel was a colonial bungalow on a one-acre estate, with high roofs, monkey-top windows, 28 rooms, a bar and a restaurant known for appams, stew and English breakfasts. The building was razed in 2000, and Bangalore Central mall stands where it was.

title: Legend: began as a reading room for Churchill
notes: Attributed to Maya Jayapal (1997). Label as LOCAL LEGEND
story: According to Maya Jayapal's 1997 book Bangalore: The Story of a City, the site began as a reading room built for Winston Churchill. This is reported lore, not an independently verified fact.

title: Lost cinemas: Imperial (closed 1990s), Blu Moon/Diamond (1994), Galaxy (2002)
hook: Brigade Road and MG Road once had a cluster of single screens
notes: Need individual addresses before splitting into places

title: Koshy's starts as a bakery
hook: Nehru, Queen Elizabeth II and Khrushchev ate here
notes: Restaurant built 1952; still open — a 'survivor' layer
story: Koshy's began in 1940 as a bakery set up by P. O. Koshy from Kerala, and the restaurant was built next door in 1952. Jawaharlal Nehru, Queen Elizabeth II and Nikita Khrushchev have all dined here. It is still open.

title: Commercial Street in 1900
notes: From Picturesque Bangalore; Then/Now candidate
story: Commercial Street, photographed by C. H. Doveton for the 1900 book Picturesque Bangalore. It is still one of the city's oldest and busiest shopping streets.

title: St Andrew's Kirk built
notes: Also ILN 1867 engraving + 1867 plan
story: St Andrew's, the Presbyterian 'Kirk' of the Cantonment, dates from 1866 and followed Scottish customs, down to Burns Night. Photographed around 1890 by Bourne and Shepherd.

title: Mission Chapel between St Andrew's and St Paul's
hook: The oldest image in the set — 1839
notes: Placement along Infantry Road approximate; road renamed 2004

title: The Residency
hook: The Governor's home was the British Residency
notes: First floor added 1967
story: Today's Lok Bhavan, formerly Raj Bhavan, was the Bangalore Residency. After independence the Maharaja chose not to live here, and it became a state guesthouse before becoming the governor's residence. Originally single-storeyed, it gained a first floor in 1967. Pictured in 1894.

title: Vidhana Soudha completed; Churchill remark shaped its style
hook: A Churchill remark about Gandhi pushed the government toward Dravidian architecture
notes: Released prisoners worked on construction
story: Vidhana Soudha was completed in 1956. By its recorded history, Churchill's 1931 description of Gandhi as a 'half-naked fakir' led the state government to choose a Dravidian style for the new legislature. Some of its builders were prisoners, released once the work was finished.

title: Ulsoor Tank with Kempe Gowda tower
notes: Also 1917 MacGeorge twilight
story: Ulsoor Tank with the Kempe Gowda tower, photographed in 1902 for Col. James Henry Erskine Reid's album of Indian views.

title: Church founded at the far end of South Parade
notes: Established 1850 per St Mark's article; Wikidata 1851
story: Holy Trinity was established at the far end of South Parade from St Mark's, around 1850-51. The Church of South India's Mysore Diocese gave it the name Holy Trinity Church in 1965. Pictured in 1922.

title: Foundation stone of current building
notes: Club founded 1868 by B. L. Rice; stone laid 22 Nov 1888
story: Bowring Institute was founded in 1868 by Benjamin Lewis Rice and named after Lewin Bentham Bowring. The foundation stone of its present 12-acre property on St Mark's Road was laid on 22 November 1888.

title: Bible and Tract Depot (1890) — still a Tract & Book Society
hook: Same organisation, same road, 136 years later
notes: Then/Now pair exists on Commons; confirm same site

title: India's first KFC opens
hook: India's very first KFC was on Brigade Road (June 1995)
notes: Wikipedia unsourced sentence — needs second source
